newsitem.title: UK: Safeway at 3-1/2 year high on banking move.
newsitem.headline: Safeway at 3-1/2 year high on banking move.

text.p: Shares in Safeway Plc rose to a 3-1/2 year high on Thursday after the supermarket operator said it was expanding into financial services through a tie-up with Abbey National Plc.
Safeway shares were up 9p at 389 by 1007 GMT, the highest since March 1993 when its was called Argyll Group, while Abbey National were up 2-1/2p at 688, after earlier setting a near-record 689p.
Under the deal, Safeway will link its loyalty card with Abbey's banking services.

Analysts said the deal was a positive long-term move but said latest figures on market shares from industry research group AGB, plus continued reaction to last week's better-than- expected results, also helped lift Safeway shares.

Analysts said AGB figures showed Safeway market share in value terms increasing to 10.9 percent from 10.4 percent the month before. "The Abbey National deal continues to show Safeway wants to be at the forefront of marketing in the sector," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.

He said the AGB figures came after Safeway's good results last week. "There has generally been some buying of Safeway shares and the market is a bit short of stock, and all that has pushed the price higher."
Bill Myers, analyst at Williams de Broe, said the Abbey National deal should be seen as an extension of Safeway's customer service.
"We have been saying the same thing for much of the year," Myers said. "The strongest and most customer-focused of the sector are Tesco and Safeway."
